text.p: Brazilian state-owned long distance telephone monopoly Embratel, a unit of the federal Telebras system, released the following 11-month 1996 earnings figures.
Note: Figures are in Brazlian reais.
Share net is per lot of 1,000 shares.
Embratel said in a report that its net profit surged 56.48 percent in the January-November period compared with the same 11 months of 1995.
It said its net worth rose to 5.543 billion reais in the 11-month period from 4.913 billion a year ago.
It said gross operating revenues reached 2.163 billion reais, up 44.2 percent from 1.5 billion reais a year ago.
Embratel, one of Telebras's 28 subsidiaries, is expected to be sold off later this year under the sweeping privatization of Brazil's telecommunications sector.
The statement said the company reduced its workforce to 11,344 employees by the end of November, down 5.43 percent from a year earlier.
The firm paid 487.5 million reais in federal, state and municipal taxes during January-November, up from 314.5 million reais a year earlier, it said.
